STEP 1 - Vessel type: The vessel is a white, flat-bottomed paper plate with a rim band and a flat centre, no inner wall visible. Flat plate (paper).

STEP 2 - Vessel size:
a) Type cue: a small-to-medium paper plate, roughly 15-18 cm (small) or 22-26 cm (large).
b) Reference object: almonds are 2.3 cm long. Across the plate, the almonds in the centre row span about 6 almonds lying end to end, from the left edge of the pile to the right edge. The pile occupies roughly 6-7 almond lengths of the plate's diameter at its widest, with a visible rim beyond the nuts on each side. The rim spans about 2.5-3 almond lengths beyond the pile on each side, giving about 14-16 almond lengths total... Using the nut pile itself as the reference, the plate diameter is about 2.3 x 6.5 pile-lengths scaled up, so roughly 16-17 cm. Reconciling with the paper-plate cue (15-18 cm), I take width = 17 cm.

Area = 0.785 x 17^2 = 227 cm².

STEP 3 - Food items:
- Almonds (countable): visible count is about 30. Items are in a loose single layer with some overlap, so add about 3 hidden under others: ~33 almonds x 1.2 g = 40 g.

Thickness check: nuts stacked up to 2 pieces deep at the thickest point, so the pile is well under 1 cm average. Layer approach is not needed since counting is used.

STEP 4 - Hidden food: no base layer visible; the plate is bare beneath the nuts. No hidden layer added.

STEP 5 - kcal per 100 g: almonds raw/dry-roasted ≈ 580-600 kcal per 100 g. Use 580.

Total: 40 g almonds, about 232 kcal.
